extracted.subtask_description: Rules and methods for developing functions into power series (Maclaurin/Taylor), testing convergence and using series to resolve indeterminate forms, plus systematic methods for integrating rational, trigonometric, and certain algebraic differentials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maclaurin (binomial) expansion
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply Maclaurin's formula to expand (1 + x)^m for any real m: derivatives f^(p)(0) = m(m-1)...(m-p+1), leading to the generalized binomial series.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write coefficients using falling factorials m(m-1)...; the series is the extended binomial theorem. Use differentiation/integration relations and initial values to fix constants when verifying. Example: compute f^(p)(0) and assemble series.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convergence criterion for binomial series
rubrics_metrics.description: The ratio of successive terms in the binomial series tends to -x as p→∞, so the series converges for |x|<1 and diverges for |x|>1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify convergence by taking the ratio of term x^(p+1) coefficient to x^p coefficient. When |x|<1 the series sum equals (1+x)^m in the symmetric interval; otherwise it diverges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification that a power series equals the function
rubrics_metrics.description: To show a series equals the function in its convergence interval, differentiate/ manipulate the series to obtain a differential relation satisfied by the function and the series, then determine constants using values at a point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiply/differentiate series to identify differentials of known functions, integrate to get equality up to a constant, then set x to a convenient value (often 0) to determine constants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taylor series via change of variable
rubrics_metrics.description: To expand f(x) about a point a, set x = a + x' and apply Maclaurin to φ(x')=f(a+x'); Taylor's formula then expresses f(a+x') in powers of x' with coefficients f^(k)(a)/k!.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Necessary and sufficient condition: φ(x') must be developable by Maclaurin. The resulting Taylor series converges for x in an interval (a - R, a + R) symmetric about a (where R is the Maclaurin radius for φ).

rubrics_metrics.name: Region of validity for Taylor/Maclaurin expansions
rubrics_metrics.description: A Taylor (or Maclaurin) expansion represents the function only within a certain symmetric interval around the expansion point determined by convergence of the series.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State explicitly the interval of convergence when giving a series (e.g., |x|<1 for many binomial/arc-sin series). Use ratio/root tests or known singularities to find radius.

rubrics_metrics.name: Series expansion of arcsin and similar integrals
rubrics_metrics.description: Obtain expansions for arc functions by choosing appropriate m in the binomial series (e.g., m = 1/2), expanding (1 - x^2)^{-1/2}, then integrating term-by-term to get arcsin series.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Change variable signs as needed, integrate from 0 to x to obtain arcsin(x) = x + x^3/(2·3) + 1·3 x^5/(2·4·5) + ...; specify interval |x|<1 and range of arcsin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method of undetermined coefficients for power series
rubrics_metrics.description: When computing the first terms of a function's power series, assume a polynomial/truncated series with unknown coefficients and determine them by matching parity and multiplying by known expansions (e.g., sin x and cos x).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exploit symmetry (odd/even) to exclude terms (e.g., tan x is odd so only odd powers appear). Multiply series, equate coefficients of like powers, and solve linear equations for coefficients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use series to resolve indeterminate forms 0/0
rubrics_metrics.description: For limits of the form 0/0, expand numerator and denominator in Taylor series about the point, cancel the lowest common power of (x-a) and take the limit of the simplified quotient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is equivalent in many cases to repeated application of L'Hôpital's rule. Example: expand (ln(1+x) - x)/x^2 etc., divide by leading powers and let x→0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling (1+x)^{1/x} and similar exponential indeterminacies
rubrics_metrics.description: For forms that tend to e or involve expressions like (1+x)^{1/x}, use log expansion: take logarithms, expand the log (or exponent) in series, then exponentiate the limit of the log to obtain the limit of the original expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replace complicated exponentials by e^{limit of exponent}. Expand ln(1 + x) and use series for small x to compute limit, then exponentiate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treating forms 0·∞ and 0^0, ∞^0, etc.
rubrics_metrics.description: Transform products of a factor tending to 0 and another to ∞ into quotient or exponential form (via logarithms) to reduce to 0/0 or ∞/∞ types; use substitutions (e.g., x = 1/t) when convenient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: if x→0 and factor behaves like t e^{-t} with t→∞, substitute t = 1/x and analyze the transformed limit; use series or known limits for e^{-t}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction to elementary integral types by substitution
rubrics_metrics.description: Given ∫f(x) dx, first check whether a change u = u(x) reduces the integral to one of elementary types (table integrals), particularly if numerator is (up to constant) derivative of denominator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If numerator equals derivative of denominator (up to factor), set u = denominator and integrate as ∫du/u^n or ln|u|. Examples: recognize d( x^3 + ... ) in numerator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial fraction decomposition for rational integrals
rubrics_metrics.description: Decompose a rational function R(x) = P(x)/Q(x) into a polynomial part plus partial fractions based on the factorization of Q(x) (real linear factors and irreducible quadratics), then integrate term-by-term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute polynomial (long) division if deg P ≥ deg Q. Factor denominator (find roots). Use undetermined coefficients to find constants of partial fractions; integrate each standard term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of partial-fraction terms and integration rules
rubrics_metrics.description: After decomposition you obtain: (I) polynomial part (integrate directly), (II) terms from real root a of multiplicity r: A/(x-a), A'/(x-a)^2,... (integrals give logs and power laws), (III) terms from irreducible quadratic (x^2+px+q)^n of the form (M x + N)/(...)^k (integrate via square completion and recurrence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For (II) integrate powers to get (x-a)^{-m+1}/(−m+1) or logs for m=1. For (III) complete the square, use substitution t and derive recurrence relations to reduce exponent n step by step, ending in arctan/log terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration with irreducible quadratic factors: complete the square and recur
rubrics_metrics.description: For integrals of (M x + N)/(x^2 + p x + q)^n, decompose numerator into derivative part plus constant, complete the square in denominator, change variable and use integration by parts to derive a recurrence reducing n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write denominator as (x + p/2)^2 + A. Split numerator accordingly, perform substitution to get integrals of powers of (t^2 + A)^(-n) and use recurrence (explicit formula given in text) to reduce to n=1, which yields arctan/log forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divide numerator when deg numerator ≥ deg denominator
rubrics_metrics.description: If degree(P) ≥ degree(Q) in P(x)/Q(x), perform polynomial division to obtain a polynomial plus a proper fraction before applying partial fractions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This yields the 'partie entière' polynomial whose integral is immediate; then decompose remaining proper fraction into partial fractions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weierstrass substitution for integrals R(sin x, cos x)
rubrics_metrics.description: To integrate a rational function of sin x and cos x, use t = tan(x/2) with sin x = 2t/(1+t^2), cos x = (1−t^2)/(1+t^2), dx = 2 dt/(1+t^2) to convert the integral into a rational integral in t.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After substitution the integrand is rational in t; integrate by partial fractions. This is the standard method for rational trig integrands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condition for a rational function of sin and cos to be rational in tan
rubrics_metrics.description: A rational function R(sin x, cos x) is rational in tan x iff it is invariant under x ↦ x + π (i.e., does not change when x is increased by π).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Necessity: tan(x) invariant under x→x+π. Sufficiency: if R is invariant then it contains only even powers of cos x and can be expressed rationally in tan x using cos^2 = 1/(1+tan^2). Use this to choose simpler substitution u = tan x when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration of rational functions in tan x
rubrics_metrics.description: If the integrand is rational in tan x (or can be rewritten so), set u = tan x and use dx = du/(1+u^2) to reduce to rational integration in u.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After substitution, integrate the resulting rational function by partial fractions as usual. This is often simpler than the Weierstrass substitution when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use trig product-to-sum identities for products of sines/cosines
rubrics_metrics.description: Convert products like cos(ax + α) cos(bx + β) into sums using identities (e.g., cosA cosB = (1/2)[cos(A+B)+cos(A−B)]) and integrate the resulting cosines directly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be mindful of special cases when a±b = 0; handle those separately (integrals reduce to cos^2 or constant factors leading to simple forms).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application examples and geometric substitutions
rubrics_metrics.description: For applied integrals (e.g., area of a sector in polar coordinates), choose substitutions suggested by the geometry (e.g., t = tan(θ/2)) and integrate using the rational-trig methods above.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Express r and dS in terms of θ, transform the integral via trig substitution, and evaluate limits carefully (e.g., lower limit 0 when sector starts at angle 0).
